does: Rubs firm food against a rough surface to turn it into fine shreds.

intro.what: Grating rubs firm food against a rough surface to make fine shreds.
intro.why: It teaches you to control texture and stop before the remaining piece becomes difficult to hold.

how: Chill a soft cheese first, so that it shreds and does not smear.
Hold the grater steady on the board or over a bowl.
Push the food down the grater in long strokes with the flat of your hand.
Stop while there is still enough left to hold.

cues.text: Loose, separate shreds that do not clump.

mistakes.mistake: Grating the last small piece and catching a knuckle.
mistakes.fix: Stop early and chop the end with a knife.

quiz.question: What should grating produce?
quiz.because: The rough grating surface breaks firm food into fine shreds.

quiz.question: How can you help soft cheese grate cleanly?
choices: Press it harder as it smears.
quiz.because: Chilling soft cheese helps it shred instead of smearing on the grater.

quiz.question: Which appearance suggests clean grating?
choices: A compressed clump without visible shreds.
quiz.because: Separate shreds show the food is cutting against the grater rather than smearing.

quiz.question: Only a small hard-to-hold end remains. What would you do?
choices: Keep grating with fingertips against the teeth.
Press the last piece harder with your knuckles.
Stop grating and chop the end with a knife.
quiz.because: Stop while enough remains to hold; chop the end instead of chasing it down the grater.
